facts.fact_text: On 19 July 1989 the applicant joined an anti-Turkish demonstration in the Ayios Kassianos area in Nicosia.
According to an affidavit sworn by the applicant before the Nicosia District Court on 3 January 2000, the demonstration of 19 July 1989 was peaceful.
The demonstrators gathered at the Ayios Kassianos school in Nicosia.

After United Nations soldiers had shouted a warning to the demonstrators not to advance further, the applicant was seized by the hair by Turkish military personnel and/or other personnel acting under Turkish control.
The applicant was beaten and assaulted by Turkish military personnel and/or other personnel acting under Turkish control.
The beating of the applicant was inflicted with electrical batons by 3 or 4 policemen all over the applicant's body, in particular the head and back.
One of the blows to the applicant caused a painful injury to the applicant's right arm and elbow, with loss of blood.
Later on 20 July 1989, after being subjected to a body search, the applicant was taken to a court which remanded her in custody for two days.
The applicant was transferred with other women who had been arrested at the same time to the Ortakeuy prison.
The applicant went on hunger strike while detained at the Ortakeuy prison.

Chapter 155, section 14(1)(b) of the Cypriot Criminal Procedure Law states that any officer may, without warrant, arrest any person who commits in his presence any offence punishable with imprisonment.
Chapter 155, section 14(1)(c) of the Cypriot Criminal Procedure Law states that any officer may, without warrant, arrest any person who obstructs a police officer while in the execution of his duty.

Section 9 of Law No. 5/72 states that any person who enters a prohibited military area without authorization, or by stealth, or fraudulently, shall be tried by a military court in accordance with the Military Offences Act, and those found guilty shall be punished.
Subsection 12(1) of the Aliens and Immigration Law states that no person shall enter or leave the Colony except through an approved port.

Subsection 12(5) of the Aliens and Immigration Law states that any person who contravenes or fails to observe any of the provisions of subsections (1), (2), (3) or (4) of section 12 shall be guilty of an offence and shall be liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or to a fine not exceeding one hundred pounds or to both such imprisonment and fine.
The Government alleged that the applicant had participated in a violent demonstration with the aim of enflaming anti-Turkish sentiment.
The Government alleged that the demonstrators, supported by the Greek-Cypriot administration, were demanding that the 'Green Line' in Nicosia should be dismantled.
The Government alleged that some demonstrators carried Greek flags, clubs, knives and wire-cutters.
The Government alleged that the demonstrators were acting in a provocative manner and shouting abuse.
The Government alleged that the demonstrators were warned in Greek and English that unless they dispersed they would be arrested in accordance with the laws of the 'TRNC'.
As a result of the beating described in the applicant's account, three of the applicant's vertebrae were damaged.
Doctors told the applicant that the condition of her central nerve was continuously deteriorating and that no surgery could be carried out.
The Government alleged that it was possible that some of the demonstrators had hurt themselves in the confusion or in attempting to scale barbed wire or other fencing.
